conclusion.direction: L^µ_X ≡ L^µ_Y iff µ_X = c·µ_Y — the equality case of the ≤_MRLAI preorder (both directions of the order hold)

ambiguity: Equality characterization rather than a strict ordering; it underpins the antisymmetry discussion of ≤_MRLAI on p.40 (with µ_X(0+) = µ_Y(0+) and τ_X = τ_Y it yields identical distributions).

quote: Theorem 3.1. Let n ≥ 1, and let X1, . . . , Xn be i.i.d. absolutely continuous lifetime random variables over the support with common differentiable survival function F̄_X, and MRL function µ_X(t) = a + bt, 0 ≤ t < τ_X, where a > 0 and b > −1. If X_{1:n} = min{X1, . . . , Xn}, then L^µ_{X_{1:n}}(t) = L^µ_X(t), 0 < t < τ_X.
family: iid components, linear MRL µ_X = a + bt (a > 0, b > −1)
compared: series-system lifetime X_{1:n} vs component lifetime X under the MRLAI function

hypotheses.text: Xi iid absolutely continuous, differentiable F̄_X, µ_X = a + bt with a > 0, b > −1

conclusion.direction: L^µ_{X_{1:n}}(t) = L^µ_X(t) for all n ≥ 1 — series system is MRLAI-equal to its component (equality case of ≤_MRLAI)

quantifiers: n ≥ 1; 0 < t < τ_X (τ_X = −a/b when b < 0; infinite when b ≥ 0)
ambiguity: Exact invariance only within the linear-MRL family — the text notes preservation of DMRLAI/IMRLAI follows for this family; the general DMRLAI class is not closed under series systems (Counterexample 3.3).
